top.title: Puka Nacua injured on Rams’ final offensive snap in win
top.description: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) catches a pass for a touchdown during an NFL football game against the Washington Commanders, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, in Landover, Maryland. | Daniel Kucin Jr. The Los Angeles Rams have dealt with a range of injuries this season, and their final offensive snap in a 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders Sunday brought more news on that front. Star Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua injured his knee on the team’s final offensive snap on a 5-yard carry with just under two minutes to play, ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo . All-Pro WR Puka Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap today, and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury, per @MikeGarafolo and me. The team does not believe he suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more. pic.twitter.com/S264w2Fe0A — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 8, 2026 After Nacua’s third-down carry didn’t pick up a first down and led to a Los Angeles punt, the Rams defense stopped a Commanders drive that reached deep into Los Angeles territory as time expired to earn the win. ESPN reported that Nacua will undergo an MRI Monday to determine the severity of the injury, though the Rams believe he did not tear his ACL. Prior to the injury, Nacua, the former BYU and Orem High star, was having another standout day. He caught 14 passes on 19 targets from Matthew Stafford for 150 receiving yards, and Nacua also caught the go-ahead touchdown with 12:51 remaining on a 7-yard catch in the corner of the end zone. INSANE TOUCHDOWN CATCH FROM PUKA NACUA 🤯 📺 @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/2cNavRnTCJ — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 8, 2026 That gave the Rams a 20-13 lead, and Los Angeles kept Washington from tying the game. Nacua has dealt with multiple injuries this year and has already missed two games this season. Despite this, the All-Pro has 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns on the year. He is currently seventh in the NFL in receiving yards with Sunday’s effort. Last year, Nacua led the league in receptions and finished second in receiving yards, behind only Seattle’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

top.title: Meriden-born NFL player John Jenkins of Baltimore Ravens visits North Haven police
top.description: Baltimore Ravens player John Jenkins from the NFL, a native of Meriden, visits with officers at the North Haven Police Department on Sunday. (Courtesy of the North Haven Police Department) NORTH HAVEN - What to do a when one of the NFL's longest-tenured defensive linemen pays your police department a visit? This was the position North Haven officers found themselves in Sunday when the Connecticut-born Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle John Jenkins came to call. "No big deal. Just another day at North Haven PD," the department posted Sunday afternoon along with photos. The 6-foot-3, 360-pound Jenkins, 37, was born and raised in Meriden. He starred as a defensive lineman for Maloney High School's Spartans, later earned a scholarship to play for the University Georgia and then entered the NFL as a third-round draft pick by the New Orleans Saints in 2013. Wearing Nike slippers and a hoodie, Jenkins struck a pose with officers who tried "to play it cool," North Haven police said. "Not everyone gets a visit like this. Just saying." The department on Sunday night said Jenkins grew up with one of North Haven's police officers, happened to be in the area and stopped by to say hello. Jenkins was able to be in Connecticut on a football Sunday because the Ravens already played Jacksonville on Thursday night in this week's schedule. top.title: The good, the bad, the s—t that gets you beat from Patriots vs. Packers
top.description: Ahead of his first training camp as Patriots head coach in 2025, Mike Vrabel explained that he was judging his team’s performances by three distinct categories: the good, the bad, and the s—t that gets you beat. If Vrabel looks at his team through those specific categorizations, we shall follow his lead. The New England Patriots were thoroughly dominated on Sunday by the Green Bay Packers. Despite both teams entering the game with identical 5-3 records, only one looked the part. The other, meanwhile, struggled from start to finish and ultimately suffered one of its worst losses in recent memory. With that said, let’s dive into our breakdown of the good — sort of — and the not-so-good from the 45-27 loss at Gillette Stadium . The good: Rare opportunities We typically try to be positive around these parts of the world wide web, but the glass is nowhere near to half full coming out of Sunday’s game. The search for anything good from the contest therefore has to yield some creative results. So, how about this: the Patriots were able to get some of their lesser-used player some increased playing time. Whether it was backup quarterback Tommy DeVito or multiple special teamers, they all got some rare in-game reps courtesy of the blowout defeat. Of course, given that New England suffered multiple injuries, they might need those backups to step up in the coming weeks. The bad: Star players One common theme for the Patriots on Sunday was their best players not holding up their end of the bargain: quarterback Drake Maye and cornerback Christian Gonzalez had rough days, to say the least. Maye seemingly reverted to his early-season self, tossing three more interceptions to contribute to Green Bay pulling away seemingly from the get-go. His first pass of the day already set the tone: an apparent miscommunication with wide receiver Mack Hollins, who returned from a four-game injury absence, led to an uncontested interception that was returned all the way to the New England 9-yard line. Two plays later, the Packers were up 7-0. That was the opening of the floodgates for the team and its quarterback. Maye finished 21-of-38 for 299 yards with three touchdowns and interceptions apiece. He finished with -0.13 expected points added per play. Gonzalez, meanwhile, played the worst game of his career. The highest-paid cornerback in football was in the area or in direct coverage on multiple big plays. While not all of the blame might fall directly on him — whether it was bracket coverage not working as intended, communication breakdowns, or defensive calls asking him to give some cushion underneath — the bottom line remains: he didn’t play up to his abilities. Unfortunately for the Patriots if their best players don’t do so, be they Maye or Gonzalez, winning is hard to come by. But we needed him to be, you know, be more aggressive for himself.” In six games since Edwards’ injury, Ball is averaging 19.7 points per game on 61% true shooting, per Stathead. top.title: Lexi Thompson Shows Pregnant Golf is Hard, but Not Impossible
top.description: Albane Valenzuela, left, and Lexi Thompson of Motor City Golf Club laugh during WTGL Media Day at SoFi Center in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida on September 20, 2026. Lexi Thompson will play while six months pregnant in the Women’s TGL’s opening season, a move that forces major changes to her swing and equipment. The 31-year-old LPGA champion announced in August that she and her husband Max Provost are expecting their first child, a girl due in February. This timing puts her right in the middle of the new league’s first six weeks of matches. The league launches on Sunday with a match between Michelle Wie West’s Los Angeles Golf Club and Lydia Ko’s New York Golf Club at 3 p.m. on ESPN. Thompson, who plays for Detroit’s Motor City Golf Club, will not be hitting balls in every match. She aims to play her debut on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 8 p.m. against Los Angeles Golf Club. That game will feature her against Wie West, Aki Iwai, and Kiara Romero. Thompson acknowledges the physical challenge of swinging a club while carrying a baby. She watched Madelene Sagstrom, who played the Dow Championship in June at 27 weeks pregnant, and was impressed by the Swedish player’s form. In September at the WTGL media day, “Her swing looked incredible,” Thompson stated. “I’m sure it’s difficult. It’s something to plan around for sure. The next few months might be very challenging for me.” Sagstrom had to change all her clubs and constantly adjust her putting stroke to handle the extra weight. She wondered how to position her body over the ball. “Do I go a little bit more on top of the belly now or go around it?” she said about the best way to be successful on the green. “You get away from that perfect golf, and just be a little bit more flexible.” Thompson faces similar choices as she prepares for her Nov. 19 appearance. Even if she misses some matches, Thompson remains committed to the league’s mission. She plans to stay involved through the first season, whether on the floor or in the owner’s box. “If I play all the matches or if I just play one, just to be able to grow the game, that’s what it’s all about,” said Thompson, who is playing for Detroit’s Motor City Golf Club, according to the Palm Beach Post . She believes the indoor format brings unique technology to the sport that fans rarely see. “Hitting inside and into a big screen, all the technology, all the numbers that are involved,ved and hitting off real grass inside, we don’t get that opportunity very often,” she said. The league operates under the same team names as the men’s TGL, including Motor City, Boston Common, New York, Atlanta Drive, and Los Angeles. Motor City will play again on Nov. 16, giving Thompson that knowledge for at least one, and possibly more, WTGL matches. The final two matches for Motor City are on Nov. 29 and Dec. 1. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams suffered another potential setback along the offensive line as Steve Avila entered Sunday’s matchup against the Washington Commanders dealing with a hamstring injury. Avila appeared to be trending in the right direction throughout the week, initially participating in a limited practice Wednesday before upgrading to full participation Thursday and Friday. His progress allowed him to avoid a game designation on the final injury report, giving the Rams optimism that their starting left guard would be available without limitations. However, those concerns resurfaced Sunday. Avila exited during the second quarter after appearing to aggravate his hamstring while blocking on a Kyren Williams rushing attempt. He was escorted to the locker room by trainers and subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the game. top.title: Former Michigan QB J.J. McCarthy Returns From Hip Scare
top.description: Former Michigan Wolverines quarterback J.J. McCarthy was making his second consecutive start for the New York Giants on Sunday, and it nearly ended early in Philadelphia. With 12:02 left in the third quarter and the Giants trailing 8-6 , McCarthy ran for three yards and Eagles linebacker Zack Baun caught him from behind. He left with a hip injury, and Jameis Winston came on in relief. The Giants listed McCarthy as questionable to return after he exited the game . He spent the drive in the locker room, tossing a football to keep warm while Winston worked, and he was back under center on New York’s next possession. Baun hurt his back on the same play and was ruled questionable himself. New York Giants quarterback JJ McCarthy, is shown during pregame practice, Sunday, October 4, 2026, in East Rutherford. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) J.J. McCarthy Credits the Giants Training Staff After New York’s 19-11 win, McCarthy handed the credit for the quick turnaround to the people who patched him up. “I can’t thank the training staff enough for helping me get back on the field as fast as possible,” he said . Giants coach John Harbaugh liked what the return said about his quarterback. “That’s big to fight through that kind of thing, fight through an injury, go back in, take care of it, get back out there,” Harbaugh said. McCarthy’s Day Before and After the Hip Injury McCarthy finished 12-of-19 for 127 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions, and he ran four times for 22 yards. His longest carry, an 11-yarder, came after he returned. He was sacked five times. Winston went 6-of-8 for 71 yards in relief and threw the game’s lone touchdown, to Isaiah Likely, which put New York ahead 13-8 in the third quarter. Giants Host Washington on a Short Week New York hosts the Washington Commanders on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video, a three-day turnaround. The Giants are 5-2-1 and lead the NFC East; Washington is 2-5-1. McCarthy said afterward that the hip was feeling good and that he would do his best to be ready for Thursday. A short week leaves a hip very little time to settle down, and if it holds him out, Winston would most likely get the start.

top.title: 2027: APC chieftain laments 73% voter apathy in Aramoko
top.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and member of the President Bola Tinubu/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, Engineer Atinuke Owolabi, has expressed concern over the low voter turnout in Aramoko-Ekiti during the 2023 presidential election, saying about 73 per cent of registered voters in the community did not participate. Owolabi, who is also the convener of PBAT-MOB Aramoko Community Engagement, spoke during an APC voter education exercise and community engagement in Aramoko, Ekiti Central Senatorial District, over the weekend. The programme, organised in support of the re-election bids of President Tinubu and Senate Leader, Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, was held under the theme, “My Vote, My Voice”. She also represents the South-West as a member of the North Central Development Commission. Owolabi said voter education was essential to strengthening democracy, particularly in rural communities where inadequate information about electoral procedures could discourage participation or lead to invalid votes. Presenting figures from the 2023 presidential election, she said Ekiti State had 988,923 registered voters, out of whom 315,058 were accredited, while 308,171 valid votes were recorded and 6,301 ballots were rejected. She said available ward-level records for Aramoko I and Aramoko II showed a combined 17,426 registered voters, compared with 4,680 votes reportedly cast during the presidential election. According to her, the figures indicated that approximately 12,746 registered voters did not participate, representing about 73 per cent of the electorate in the two wards. She urged residents to improve their participation in future elections, stressing the need for the community to translate its voting strength into meaningful democratic engagement. Owolabi said the exercise was designed to educate residents on voting procedures, encourage participation and reduce the number of rejected ballots. The programme also featured the unveiling of a voter education handbook intended to guide residents on electoral processes, identification of polling units and the proper use of their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). She said: “I believe voter education is key. If we cannot completely eliminate rejected votes, we should at least be able to reduce them in Ekiti State, particularly in Aramoko, my community. “We are here to sensitise our people on the correct way to vote. When they go to the polling units, they must ensure that they vote correctly. “We have the population, and we have the voters. What is really lacking is adequate information. top.title: Jared Goff Reveals the Question Lions Asked Themselves During an Emotional Week
top.description: The Detroit Lions picked up their fourth consecutive victory Sunday afternoon, defeating the Miami Dolphins 19-9 to improve to 6-2 on the season. But following the win, quarterback Jared Goff revealed that getting ready for Sunday’s game wasn’t nearly as simple as preparing for another NFL opponent. After watching teammate Jack Campbell suffer a frightening neck injury against Minnesota one week earlier, the Lions faced an emotional challenge that went far beyond football. According to Goff, the team eventually rallied around one important question that helped everyone refocus. “What would he want? How would he want us to play?” Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) makes a pass Miami Dolphins during the second half at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jared Goff Reveals How Lions Handled Emotional Week During his postgame press conference following Sunday’s victory , Goff acknowledged how difficult it was for Detroit’s players to return their attention to football while Campbell remained hospitalized. “I think all week, certainly early in the week, it was really hard to kind of get your mind back into what we have to do. Certainly for those guys on defense, he’s their nucleus. To be able to come back to work and work the way they did, and then play the way they did, and us as a team kind of rallying around each other and leaning on each other a little bit.” Goff explained that the Lions eventually began approaching the situation by considering what their injured teammate would expect from them. “It was hard. It was hard. But I think as the week went on, you start to think about, ‘What would he want? How would he want us to play?’” And according to Goff, the answer wasn’t particularly complicated. Campbell would want his teammates focused on doing their jobs rather than spending their time feeling sorry for him. “He wouldn’t even want us talking about him right now. He wouldn’t want us doing all this stuff about how we’re going to play for him. He wouldn’t want any of that. But he’s a special guy to us and means a lot.” Those comments offer another glimpse into the impact Campbell has made inside Detroit’s locker room. As previously reported by Detroit Sports Nation , Goff has been among the players publicly expressing their support for the injured linebacker throughout the week. Lions Defense Answers the Call Against Miami If Sunday’s performance was any indication, Detroit’s defense certainly took that message to heart. Despite missing its defensive captain, the Lions held Miami without a touchdown and surrendered just 182 total yards. According to the official game recap , rookie Derrick Moore recorded two sacks, Chuck Clark intercepted a pass, and Detroit limited the Dolphins to just four third-down conversions on 12 attempts. nigeria.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and member of the President Bola Tinubu/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, Engineer Atinuke Owolabi, has expressed concern over the low voter turnout in Aramoko-Ekiti during the 2023 presidential election, saying about 73 per cent of registered voters in the community did not participate. Owolabi, who is also the convener of PBAT-MOB Aramoko Community Engagement, spoke during an APC voter education exercise and community engagement in Aramoko, Ekiti Central Senatorial District, over the weekend. The programme, organised in support of the re-election bids of President Tinubu and Senate Leader, Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, was held under the theme, “My Vote, My Voice”. She also represents the South-West as a member of the North Central Development Commission. Owolabi said voter education was essential to strengthening democracy, particularly in rural communities where inadequate information about electoral procedures could discourage participation or lead to invalid votes. Presenting figures from the 2023 presidential election, she said Ekiti State had 988,923 registered voters, out of whom 315,058 were accredited, while 308,171 valid votes were recorded and 6,301 ballots were rejected. She said available ward-level records for Aramoko I and Aramoko II showed a combined 17,426 registered voters, compared with 4,680 votes reportedly cast during the presidential election. According to her, the figures indicated that approximately 12,746 registered voters did not participate, representing about 73 per cent of the electorate in the two wards. She urged residents to improve their participation in future elections, stressing the need for the community to translate its voting strength into meaningful democratic engagement. Owolabi said the exercise was designed to educate residents on voting procedures, encourage participation and reduce the number of rejected ballots. The programme also featured the unveiling of a voter education handbook intended to guide residents on electoral processes, identification of polling units and the proper use of their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). She said: “I believe voter education is key. If we cannot completely eliminate rejected votes, we should at least be able to reduce them in Ekiti State, particularly in Aramoko, my community. “We are here to sensitise our people on the correct way to vote. When they go to the polling units, they must ensure that they vote correctly. “We have the population, and we have the voters. What is really lacking is adequate information. Our people need to understand the right way to vote. “Today, we have unveiled a voter education handbook, which is a welcome development. nigeria.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Aba South Local Government Area of Abia State has established commercial poultry and piggery farms as part of efforts to boost its internally generated revenue (IGR), create jobs and equip residents with skills in animal husbandry. The Executive Chairman of the council, Chief Obialo Anyanwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists on his administration’s two-year achievements, explaining that the initiative was aimed at making the local government more financially self-reliant. Anyanwu said his administration was exploring sustainable revenue sources to strengthen the council’s capacity to deliver services rather than depend entirely on external funding. He explained that the farms would also serve as training centres where residents would acquire practical skills in animal farming, enabling them to establish their own businesses and employ others. He said: “We don’t believe in all these 10kg of rice empowerment. What we want in Aba South is giving our people that level of empowerment that will make them self-sustaining and employ others. So, we’re envisaging such a future. We, as the third tier of government, must stand for ourselves, and it has pushed us into doing commercial poultry and commercial pig farming.” The chairman disclosed that the poultry farm occupies 14 plots of land, while the piggery farm covers seven plots. He added that the projects would generate revenue for the council, create employment opportunities and provide practical agricultural training for residents, including staff of the council’s agriculture department. On healthcare, Anyanwu said the council had established and equipped 22 Glycoster World Primary Healthcare Centres in partnership with the Abia State Government. He said the facilities had been commissioned and made operational, adding that the council had also organised free medical tests and treatments for residents. nigeria.title: Sultan directs Muslims to sight Jumada Assaniya moon Monday
nigeria.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO – The Sultanate Council of Sokoto has called on Muslims across Nigeria to search for the new crescent moon of Jumada Assaniya 1448AH on Monday, November 9, 2026. The directive was contained in a statement dated November 8, 2026, signed by Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu and made available to journalists on Sunday. According to the statement, the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council identified Monday as the 29th day of Jumada al-Ula 1448AH and the appropriate date for the nationwide moon-sighting exercise. The council urged Muslims across the country to actively participate in the exercise by looking out for the new crescent moon after sunset on Monday. It specifically requested anyone who sights the crescent to promptly report the observation to the nearest District or Village Head for onward transmission to His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, CFR, mni, the Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA). The council stressed the importance of timely and credible reports of confirmed sightings to enable the Sultan to make the appropriate religious announcement on the commencement of the new Islamic month. It noted that the Sultan remains the recognised authority responsible for communicating the outcome of the moon-sighting exercise to Muslims across the country. The announcement underscores the role of the Sultanate Council in coordinating Islamic religious affairs and guiding the Muslim Ummah on matters concerning the Islamic lunar calendar. In a prayer, Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu, Waziri and Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council, asked Allah (SWT) to grant Muslims the guidance and strength to discharge the religious responsibility successfully. The council also prayed for divine assistance and acceptance of the exercise, urging Muslims to approach the assignment with sincerity, vigilance and a strong sense of religious commitment. nigeria.title: Fermin brace earns Liga leaders Barcelona 2-1 win at Atletico
nigeria.description: Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 and move three points clear at the top of La Liga. The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, with Atletico third, now five points behind. Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium. The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in. The match started at a fast pace and both teams hit the woodwork in the opening stages. Alvarez, who tried and failed to force a move from Atletico to Barca in the summer, rounded goalkeeper Joan Garcia but could not finish off the chance as the defence blocked his route to goal. From the resulting corner Atletico defender Marc Pubill headed against the crossbar with Garcia beaten. At the other end Pedri crashed a strike against the woodwork after being fed by Barca’s teenage star Lamine Yamal. Atletico took the lead in the 10th minute, slicing Barca’s defence open. Alvarez crossed for Giuliano Simeone to turn home from close range. The game settled down after that pulsating start, although Alvarez came close to scoring Atletico’s second. The Argentine international’s shot was fumbled by Garcia, but the goalkeeper was able to collect the ball quickly afterwards. Yamal blasted into the side-netting from a tight angle with Barcelona not able to click into their top gears. Despite their struggles they went in level at the break, with a goal out of nowhere. Lopez’s path to the box was blocked but the ball bounced loose to the midfielder and he quickly smashed a strike past Jan Oblak. Early in the second half Alvarez lobbed over the crossbar when running in on goal. The forward came to rue the miss when Barcelona took the lead. Yamal played a clever pass through Atletico’s defence and Lopez kept his cool to beat Oblak. It was his seventh league goal in 11 top flight appearances this season. Barcelona kept Atletico at bay well in the final stages to take three points home from the capital before the international break. nigeria.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos APC Candidate Hamzat Promises 4,000 CNG Buses, 77 Electric Ferries
nigeria.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Obafemi Hamzat, has promised to deploy 4,000 compressed natural gas (CNG) buses to move one million passengers daily as part of plans to ease transportation challenges in the state. Hamzat, the incumbent Deputy Governor, also disclosed plans to expand water transportation with 77 electric ferries and improve connectivity between different parts of Lagos through an integrated transport system. ﻿ He made the promises on Sunday during the Lagos governorship debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper. Explaining his transportation plans, Hamzat said the objective was to reduce commuting time and give residents more opportunities to rest and spend time with their families. “The plan is to give back time to the citizens to plan, to rest, to spend with their family. There’s nowhere in Africa that the private sector has funded a rail. “Since BRT started, it has done 77 million journeys; that is with 1,000 buses. My plan says we will push it to 4,000 buses; the idea is to move one million people a day with 4,000 CNG buses, meaning up to 5,000, create BRt lane from Marina to Epe, from Marina to Badagry and so on and so forth,” he said. “Today, over four million people have the Cowry card. What does that mean? It means you can use ferry, you can use rail, and you can use BRT buses — one payment — so that we can deal with how to subsidise it. On healthcare, the APC candidate promised to expand access to medical services by increasing the number of primary healthcare centres providing round-the-clock services. nigeria.title: Seven killed, over 100 injured in Egypt train collision
nigeria.description: At least seven people have been killed and more than 100 injured after two trains collided near Giza, Egypt, causing several carriages to derail and plunge down an embankment. The country’s railway authority said the trains, travelling south from Giza and Cairo, collided in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat. Egypt’s President, Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, said he had directed relevant authorities to investigate the circumstances surrounding the accident and ensure that anyone found negligent was held accountable. The public prosecutor’s office warned that the death toll could rise as rescue and recovery operations continued. The government said hospitals in the affected area had been placed on heightened alert to handle the large number of casualties. Health Minister, Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said victims were receiving treatment for various injuries, including broken bones and head injuries. The Egyptian Red Crescent also deployed personnel to provide emergency assistance and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene. The ministry confirmed that the driver of one of the trains was among those killed in the collision. According to reports, the first train was travelling from Giza to Fayoum when it crashed into the rear of another train heading from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks. Photographs from the scene showed several overturned carriages, with emergency responders and members of the public searching through the wreckage for survivors. Train services between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were deployed to remove the damaged trains. The railway authority had yet to announce when services would resume. The crash occurred close to the location of Egypt’s deadliest railway disaster, which happened in February 2002 when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor, killing more than 370 people officially, although some estimates put the death toll higher. Two other train accidents in the area in 2009 also claimed dozens of lives. The latest disaster sparked calls on Sunday for Egypt’s transport minister to resign over the recurring railway accidents. Meanwhile, foreign governments and diplomatic representatives expressed condolences and solidarity with Egypt over the tragedy. Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed solidarity with Egypt and wished the injured a speedy recovery. Turkey’s Ambassador to Egypt also conveyed his condolences on X to the victims, their families and the Egyptian people. nigeria.title: No Political Will To Deal With Agberos In Lagos, Says NDC’s Funsho Doherty
nigeria.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Lagos State, Funsho Doherty, has blamed the persistence of the agbero system in the state on a lack of political will by successive administrations to reform the transport sector. Agberos are transport touts who collect money from commercial bus drivers and other transport operators at motor parks, bus stops and along roads, often claiming to represent transport unions or park authorities. Speaking during the Lagos Governorship Debate on Sunday, Doherty said powerful interests within the existing transport system had made it difficult for successive governments to tackle the activities of the operators. The debate was organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, a coalition of five media organisations: Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard Newspapers. “Many of us understand this notion of the agbero system that people talk about. There is no political will to deal with that problem,” Doherty said. He argued that meaningful reform of public transportation would require a government that was accountable to residents rather than interests benefiting from the existing arrangement. “We will modernise the transportation system because we will be elected by the people, not by an agbero network,” he said. nigeria.title: Police arrest six suspected phone thieves at Makinde’s Bauchi rally
nigeria.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested six suspected phone thieves accused of stealing mobile phones from participants at the presidential campaign flag-off of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM) candidate, Governor Seyi Makinde, in the state. The suspects were arrested by operatives of the Police Violent Crimes Response Unit (VCRU), deployed to provide security at the campaign venue, following the detection of their suspicious movements during the event. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying exhibits were recovered from four of the suspects, while two others were identified by a victim as allegedly responsible for stealing his phone. The suspects were identified as Muhammad Rabiu, 20; Ibrahim Abubakar, 25; Hamza Usman, 18; Abba Bala, 20; Auwal Muhammad, 23; and Inusa Adamu, 20. Items recovered from them included an itel torchlight phone, an OPPO Android phone, an Infinix Smart 20 phone and a 20,000mAh power bank. The police spokesman said a Samsung Fold 4 allegedly stolen during the event had yet to be recovered, adding that efforts were being intensified to retrieve the device and other missing valuables. He said investigation was ongoing and that the suspects would be charged to court upon its conclusion. The Commissioner of Police, Sani-Omolori Aliyu, commended the operatives for their vigilance and prompt action, which led to the arrests and recovery of some stolen items. He warned criminal elements against exploiting public gatherings and political events to perpetrate crime, stressing that the command would not relent in its efforts to rid the state of criminal activities. The commissioner also urged members of the public attending political rallies and other public events to remain vigilant, safeguard their valuables and promptly report suspicious movements to security operatives. He called for continued public cooperation through the provision of timely and credible information to assist the command in preventing and controlling crime. nigeria.title: Police rescue five kidnap victims, arrest three suspects in Kebbi
nigeria.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has rescued five kidnapped victims and arrested three suspects following a coordinated security operation in Dakingari, Suru Local Government Area of the state. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman Kebbi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the operation followed credible intelligence that armed men had invaded Dolen Kwandage Village and abducted three residents. Recalling his engagement with former President Muhammadu Buhari on the issue in 2019, Makinde said the former president had expressed concerns about the ability of some states to fund their police formations. “When we approached President Buhari in 2019, one of the concerns he raised was that some states could not even pay workers’ salaries. He said the operatives gather intelligence and work with federal security agencies, adding that the initiative had helped improve security coordination in the region. Those concerns are valid, and we must put safeguards in place. “But the fact that something can be abused does not mean we should not do it. We must design a system that ensures accountability and protects the rights of the people,” he said. nigeria.title: Lagos 2027: PDP’s Deji Doherty Defends Alliance With Wike, Tinubu
nigeria.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has defended his political relationship with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, despite the latter’s support for President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC). Doherty said Wike’s position in the APC-led Federal Government does not make him an enemy of democracy, arguing that politics and democracy can accommodate different political alignments. nigeria.title: Customs processes 99,839 cargo declarations in two months
nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) processed 9,195 Pre-Arrival Assessment Reports (PAARs) and 99,839 Single Goods Declarations (SGDs) between September and October 2026, generating a combined revenue of approximately ₦1.42 trillion. The figures were disclosed during a joint security press briefing at the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), under the Office of the National Security Adviser, in Abuja. Speaking at the briefing, the National Public Relations Officer of the NCS, Deputy Comptroller Abdullahi Aliyu Maiwada, said the performance reflected the Service’s commitment to facilitating legitimate trade, improving cargo clearance and strengthening revenue generation through digital interventions and collaboration with stakeholders. A breakdown of the figures showed that the Service processed 2,102 PAARs in September and 7,093 in October, bringing the total to 9,195. Similarly, 48,832 SGDs were processed in September, while 51,007 were recorded in October, giving a combined total of 99,839 declarations. The Service collected ₦697.8 billion in revenue in September and ₦722.9 billion in October, amounting to ₦1.4207 trillion during the two-month period. In a statement, Maiwada also disclosed that the Service recorded significant progress in export trade facilitation. At the Lilypond Export Command, export activities in the third quarter of 2026 generated a total export value of $752.85 million, compared with $586.15 million recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The statement put the increase at approximately 28.44 per cent, reflecting the growing contribution of the export sector and the impact of measures aimed at facilitating non-oil exports. On enforcement, the NCS said it seized prohibited and restricted items with a combined Duty Paid Value exceeding ₦8.1 billion during the period under review. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. entertainment.title: “When Are You Coming Home?” ValueJet Restores Daily Flights to Asaba Ahead of the Festive Season
entertainment.description: Daily Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja services resume on Friday, 20 November 2026, strengthening regional connectivity and bringing families together for the holidays. Somewhere in Lagos or Abuja right now, a phone is ringing, and the voice on the other end is asking the single question that marks the true beginning of the Nigerian festive season: “When are you coming home?” For thousands of professionals, business owners, and families whose answer is Asaba and the surrounding communities across Delta and Anambra states, ValueJet has delivered timely news. The airline will officially resume daily scheduled flights on its Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja routes starting Friday, 20 November 2026, just as year-end travel planning reaches peak momentum. The end of the year carries an undeniable emotional pull back to one’s roots. It is the season of growing gift lists, overpacked suitcases, group chats buzzing with reunion itineraries, and the quiet warmth of returning to familiar streets. For many families, December represents the single period in the year when loved ones assemble under one roof. By reintroducing daily non-stop frequency on both routes, ValueJet provides critical operational flexibility for holiday travelers. Whether passengers are heading home early to spend the entire season with family or flying out closer to Christmas Eve after wrapping up the work year, the restored schedule ensures seamless travel options tailored to diverse holiday schedules. “The festive season is fundamentally about people, relationships, and shared moments. At ValueJet, our mission is to ensure that distance never stands in the way of those connections,” said Omololu Majekodunmi , Managing Director of ValueJet. “Restoring our daily services to Asaba reflects our deep commitment to serving the travel needs of our passengers during the most important time of the year. We are proud to offer a reliable, comfortable, and affordable gateway home for families and communities across the region.” The Lagos–Asaba service bridges Nigeria’s commercial capital directly with the vibrant heart of Delta State, facilitating easy access across the South-South and South-East regions. Simultaneously, the Asaba–Abuja route delivers a direct, hassle-free link between the nation’s capital and Asaba, eliminating lengthy road journeys and complex connection itineraries. The resumption complements ValueJet’s rapidly expanding domestic and regional network. Domestically, the airline provides essential air links to key destinations including Port Harcourt, Jos, Owerri, Calabar, Benin, and GWI-Iperu. Beyond Nigeria’s borders, ValueJet continues to extend its reach beyond established destinations like Accra, Banjul, Cotonou, and Malabo with upcoming regional route expansions to Libreville, Monrovia, and Abidjan. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. SHOW AND AVAILABILITY Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. We want women to leave Finance Fair knowing that they can save, invest, grow their income, build businesses and take ownership of their financial future,” she shared ahead of the event. Beyond Finance Fair, FinTribe is building a community where women learn about money and put that knowledge into practice . With a presence across 43 countries, the organisation has reached over 20,000 women through financial education, supported more than 5,000 women with capital market training and helped members collectively save and invest millions of dollars. Through its Wealth Builders Academy, savings and investment community, real estate initiatives and recently launched FinTribe App, the organisation continues to create opportunities for women to build healthier financial habits, develop investment confidence and work towards long-term financial independence. At the fair, award-winning filmmaker Omoni Oboli encouraged women to pursue their ambitions without neglecting their wellbeing, reminding them to take things one step at a time, prioritise rest and ask for help when needed. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. This was the position North Haven officers found themselves in Sunday when the Connecticut-born Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle John Jenkins came to call. "No big deal. Just another day at North Haven PD," the department posted Sunday afternoon along with photos. The 6-foot-3, 360-pound Jenkins, 37, was born and raised in Meriden. He starred as a defensive lineman for Maloney High School's Spartans, later earned a scholarship to play for the University Georgia and then entered the NFL as a third-round draft pick by the New Orleans Saints in 2013. If Vrabel looks at his team through those specific categorizations, we shall follow his lead. The New England Patriots were thoroughly dominated on Sunday by the Green Bay Packers. Despite both teams entering the game with identical 5-3 records, only one looked the part. The other, meanwhile, struggled from start to finish and ultimately suffered one of its worst losses in recent memory. With that said, let’s dive into our breakdown of the good — sort of — and the not-so-good from the 45-27 loss at Gillette Stadium . The good: Rare opportunities We typically try to be positive around these parts of the world wide web, but the glass is nowhere near to half full coming out of Sunday’s game. The search for anything good from the contest therefore has to yield some creative results. So, how about this: the Patriots were able to get some of their lesser-used player some increased playing time. Whether it was backup quarterback Tommy DeVito or multiple special teamers, they all got some rare in-game reps courtesy of the blowout defeat. Of course, given that New England suffered multiple injuries, they might need those backups to step up in the coming weeks. The bad: Star players One common theme for the Patriots on Sunday was their best players not holding up their end of the bargain: quarterback Drake Maye and cornerback Christian Gonzalez had rough days, to say the least. sports.title: Former Michigan QB J.J. McCarthy Returns From Hip Scare
sports.description: Former Michigan Wolverines quarterback J.J. McCarthy was making his second consecutive start for the New York Giants on Sunday, and it nearly ended early in Philadelphia. With 12:02 left in the third quarter and the Giants trailing 8-6 , McCarthy ran for three yards and Eagles linebacker Zack Baun caught him from behind. He left with a hip injury, and Jameis Winston came on in relief. The Giants listed McCarthy as questionable to return after he exited the game . He spent the drive in the locker room, tossing a football to keep warm while Winston worked, and he was back under center on New York’s next possession. Baun hurt his back on the same play and was ruled questionable himself. New York Giants quarterback JJ McCarthy, is shown during pregame practice, Sunday, October 4, 2026, in East Rutherford. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) J.J. McCarthy Credits the Giants Training Staff After New York’s 19-11 win, McCarthy handed the credit for the quick turnaround to the people who patched him up. “I can’t thank the training staff enough for helping me get back on the field as fast as possible,” he said . Giants coach John Harbaugh liked what the return said about his quarterback. “That’s big to fight through that kind of thing, fight through an injury, go back in, take care of it, get back out there,” Harbaugh said. McCarthy’s Day Before and After the Hip Injury McCarthy finished 12-of-19 for 127 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions, and he ran four times for 22 yards. His longest carry, an 11-yarder, came after he returned. He was sacked five times. Winston went 6-of-8 for 71 yards in relief and threw the game’s lone touchdown, to Isaiah Likely, which put New York ahead 13-8 in the third quarter. The Giants are 5-2-1 and lead the NFC East; Washington is 2-5-1. McCarthy said afterward that the hip was feeling good and that he would do his best to be ready for Thursday. A short week leaves a hip very little time to settle down, and if it holds him out, Winston would most likely get the start.

sports.description: The Detroit Lions picked up their fourth consecutive victory Sunday afternoon, defeating the Miami Dolphins 19-9 to improve to 6-2 on the season. But following the win, quarterback Jared Goff revealed that getting ready for Sunday’s game wasn’t nearly as simple as preparing for another NFL opponent. After watching teammate Jack Campbell suffer a frightening neck injury against Minnesota one week earlier, the Lions faced an emotional challenge that went far beyond football. According to Goff, the team eventually rallied around one important question that helped everyone refocus. “What would he want? How would he want us to play?” Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) makes a pass Miami Dolphins during the second half at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Certainly for those guys on defense, he’s their nucleus. To be able to come back to work and work the way they did, and then play the way they did, and us as a team kind of rallying around each other and leaning on each other a little bit.” Goff explained that the Lions eventually began approaching the situation by considering what their injured teammate would expect from them. “It was hard. It was hard. But I think as the week went on, you start to think about, ‘What would he want? How would he want us to play?’” And according to Goff, the answer wasn’t particularly complicated. science.description: null "Starlog" was one of the greatest sci-fi and fantasy magazines ever, and after a 17-year absence, it's being resurrected. The legendary sci-fi mag went dark back in 2009 as part of the wave of popular publications folding due to years of declining readership and subscriptions. But as of Nov. 13, this geek favorite periodical returns as an annual print edition, and it's available for pre-order now. It’s another indication of digital fatigue in the world, and fans of a certain age will recall the pleasure of poring over each colorful issue packed with in-depth interviews, behind-the-scenes photos, TV guides, classic movie retrospectives, book reviews, con news, and VFX features. The triumphant relaunch of "Starlog" magazine happens on Nov. 13, 2026 (Image credit: Fangoria Holdings) "Starlog" launched in 1976, in the pre-" Star Wars " days, under the leadership of editor-in-chief Terry O’Quinn. It first arrived with artist Jack Thurston's beautiful painted "Star Trek" cover, featuring William Shatner as Captain James T. Kirk and Leonard Nimoy’s Spock, set against the U.S.S. Enterprise near a shimmering black hole. The magazine continued to inform the science fiction community about upcoming sci-fi TV shows and blockbuster Hollywood films for over three decades; I fondly recall reading each informative and entertaining monthly issue cover-to-cover. Just in time to honor its 50th anniversary this year, "Starlog" blasts back into the sci-fi universe with Issue #375 showcasing cover artwork created by Armenian artist Gabriel Yeganyan. Its geek culture legacy, covering iconic franchises like "Star Wars," "Star Trek," and "Alien," will now live on thanks to Fangoria Holdings and io9 co-founder Annalee Newitz, editor-in-chief. Three vintage "Starlog" magazine issues from my personal collection! (Image credit: Jeff Spry) "During its original 33-year run, 'Starlog' documented science fiction as it evolved across film, television, books, technology, and culture," said 'Fangoria's Tara Ansley. "Fifty years after the magazine first launched, the line between science fiction and the real world has become increasingly difficult to separate. That makes this an especially interesting time to bring 'Starlog' back. Technology may change, but the most compelling questions have always been about people: how we live, what we create, and what kind of future we want to build." "Starlog" reloads for its first annual edition after a long hiatus on Nov. 13. You can pre-order the first issue (Issue 375 in continuity) on the Starlog website .

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
science.description: null On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this. It performed well, but eventually it stopped listening to commands. The spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere in January 2015. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the Venus Express spacecraft to Venus on Nov. 8, 2005.. (Image credit: ESA) Why it mattered Venus Express established ESA as the third world organization to successfully send a probe to study Venus, following the United States and Soviet Union. (Japan's JAXA became the fourth five years later.) "By studying Venus, scientists learn how Earth-like planets change over time," reads a summary of the planet's exploration prepared by The Planetary Society. "Orbital studies [like Venus Express] hint that Venus may have hosted habitable oceans before becoming inhospitable." "By studying Venus, we can learn how Earth-like planets evolve and what shapes planets throughout the galaxy into temperate, lush worlds instead of sweltering hothouses. Venus also helps scientists model Earth’s climate, and may serve as a cautionary tale on how dramatically a planet’s climate can change," wrote the Society. An illustration of the Venus Express spacecraft in orbit around Venus. (Image credit: ESA) ESA returned to Venus in 2018 when BepiColombo, its joint mission with JAXA, used the planet's gravity to redirect its path toward the planet Mercury. Want more space history? science.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
science.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. An illustration shows the landscape of a primordial Earth before life arose as lightning splits the skies (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) What makes the simulation especially useful is its plug-and-play nature. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. If the result is a planet with an atmosphere that matches what is detected spectroscopically by the James Webb Space Telescope or, in the future, the various extremely large 30-meter-plus ground-based telescopes or NASA’s planned Habitable Worlds Observatory , then we know that planet probably does not have life as we know it. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments."
